Our mission

A farm that pays for a forest.

Most reforestation is funded by people a long way from the land. We do it the other way round: the farm earns, the woodland grows, and the people who plant it live twenty minutes away.

Our farm · Our mission

Rootstock began with eleven acres of exhausted ley and a stubborn idea: that a farm could pay for the forest around it. Nine years later the farm feeds 900 households a week and the forest covers 1,840 acres.

Our story

Nine winters,
one idea.

We are not a charity that discovered farming, and not a farm that discovered marketing. We are a community interest company with an asset lock, a tractor, and 412,000 trees.

See what we planted

2016

Eleven acres and a borrowed spade

Two of us take on a failing dairy holding at Cwm Aeron. The first 3,000 trees go in that November, funded by a market stall.

2018

The nursery opens

We stop buying saplings and start growing them from seed collected within 40 miles. Cost per tree falls from £8.40 to £3.10.

2020

Boxes become forests

The veg box scheme reaches 500 households. Every subscription plants four trees a year — and always has.

2022

Neighbours join in

96 partner farms sign 100-year covenants, turning scattered corners into one connected corridor.

2026

Half a million in sight

412,000 trees planted, 94% surviving at year three, and a nursery capacity of 90,000 saplings a season.

How we work

Four practices, no shortcuts

Everything below is audited annually and published in our impact report. Where we fall short, we say so.

The carbon is in the roots

We stopped ploughing in 2017. Since then the top 30cm of our fields has gone from 3.1% to 5.4% organic matter — roughly 41 tonnes of extra carbon per hectare, held where it belongs.

  • Seven-year rotations with two years of herbal ley
  • No synthetic nitrogen since 2019
  • Compost made on-farm from green waste and woodchip
  • Sheep grazed on cover crops, never on young planting

Trees that already know this weather

Every seed is collected within 40 miles of where it will be planted, by hand, from trees we have mapped and monitored. Imported stock brings imported disease.

  • 27 native species, 90,000 saplings a year
  • Peat-free compost and reusable air-pruning trays
  • Two years in the nursery before planting out
  • Provenance recorded to a six-figure grid reference

Slow the water, hold the hill

Eleven miles of the Aeron now run through shade. Summer water temperature in the shaded reaches is 2.4°C lower, and the sediment load after heavy rain has halved.

  • Leaky dams and re-meandered ditches on 120 acres
  • Alder and willow carr on re-wetted peat
  • Fenced buffers of 12m either side of the main channel
  • Monthly invertebrate counts with the local rivers trust

Restoration is a job, not a gesture

Planting seasons employ 34 people from within 15 miles, on real contracts at the real living wage. Six apprentices a year train in nursery work, hedge-laying and coppice management.

  • Real Living Wage employer since 2019
  • Six paid apprenticeships each year
  • 1,900 volunteer days hosted last season
  • Free planting days for every local school

RiparianStarted 2019640 acres

Aeron Valley Corridor

The Aeron used to run bare and warm between two fragments of ancient woodland five miles apart. We are stitching them back together with a continuous shaded corridor of alder, willow, hazel and oak — wide enough for dormice, cool enough for trout.

82,400

Trees planted

2.4°C

Cooler in shade

96%

Year-3 survival

Alder 28%, downy birch 18%, hazel 16%, sessile oak 12%, goat willow 10%, rowan 8%, bird cherry 5%, small-leaved lime 3%. All grown from seed collected between Glasbury and Talgarth.

The 2021 winter planting on the eastern bank lost 31% of stock to voles because we skipped guards to save money. We replanted at our own cost in 2022 and now guard every riparian plot.

Fourteen separate landowners, each with a 100-year covenant registered against the title. Rootstock holds the management obligation; the landowner keeps the land.

Fund this corridor
UplandStarted 2021820 acres

Black Hill Ascent

Above 380 metres, nothing has regenerated here in eighty years of hard grazing. We took the sheep off half the hill, and are planting a graded mosaic — birch and rowan low down, juniper and montane willow at the top, open ground left deliberately open.

  • 46,900 trees planted across 61 discrete plots
  • Deer fencing on 40% of the area; the rest relies on tree guards and a culling agreement
  • Breeding curlew recorded on the unplanted mosaic for the first time since 2011
46,900 of 80,000 trees59%

Wet woodlandStarted 2023120 acres

Llyn Marsh Carr

Drained in 1974, this peat basin was losing more carbon every year than our entire planting programme captured. We blocked 4.1km of ditch, let the water table come back up, and planted only where the ground told us to.

Water table

Raised by an average of 42cm across the basin.

Emissions

Peat oxidation cut by an estimated 780 tCO₂e a year.

Half of this site will never be planted. Open water and sedge fen do more here than trees would — restoration is not the same as planting.
Support the carr

Lost Orchards Project

Forty-one Herefordshire cider and perry varieties were down to a handful of surviving trees. We graft from those survivors onto local rootstock — the practice this whole organisation is named after — and give the trees back to the farms that lost them.

Home Design system
Understory v1.0

The design system
behind the forest.

Every page on this site is assembled from the tokens and components documented here. One stylesheet, one motion vocabulary, no page-specific exceptions. Click any token to copy it.

Jump to components

Contents

Principles Colour Typography Space & radius Elevation Iconography Components Forms Motion Accessibility Using the system
01

Principles

Four rules that settle most design arguments before they start.

Earned, not decorative

Every animation, gradient and illustration has to do a job — direct attention, show state, or explain a process. Ornament that does none of those gets cut.

Legible before beautiful

Body text never falls below 16px, at any viewport width, and never below 4.5:1 contrast. If a design choice fights readability, readability wins.

One system, no exceptions

No page-specific stylesheets. If a page needs something new, it becomes a component here first.

Honest about the numbers

Data components are built to show shortfalls as clearly as successes. A progress meter at 40% must look like 40%.

02

Colour

Three families: leaf greens carry the brand, lime is the single accent reserved for action, and warm papers hold the page together. Clay appears only to represent degraded land. The greens are deliberately olive rather than emerald — the colour of a hedgerow in July, not a logo.

Forest

Lime — action only

Neutrals

Measured on the paper background: body text 16.0:1, muted text 5.4:1, breadcrumbs and footer meta 4.6:1, green buttons 6.3:1, and lime buttons carrying forest-900 text at 12.5:1. Every text pairing clears 4.5:1 in both themes. Lime is never used for text on a light surface — it fails at every size.

Semantic tokens

Components only ever reference these. Swapping the theme redefines the semantic layer, never the components.

/* light theme */
--bg: #F2F1EB; /* the paper panels sit on */
--surface: #FFFFFF;
--bg-alt: var(--sand-300);
--text: var(--ink-900);
--text-muted: var(--ink-500);
--brand: var(--forest-500);
--brand-strong: var(--forest-600);
--accent: var(--lime-500);
--border: #E7E5DB;
03

Typography

Plus Jakarta Sans carries everything — interface, headlines and figures — with an old-style serif reserved for quotations and a mono for data. It is self-hosted as a single variable file (400–800), so there are no third-party requests and no flash of fallback text. The scale is fluid: every step is a clamp(), so nothing needs a breakpoint, and body text never drops below 16px.

--step-6 · display · 2.7–5.1rem · -0.038em · word-spacing .1em

Grow forests

--step-5 · h1 · 2.35–4.35rem

A farm that pays for a forest

--step-4 · h2 · 1.95–3.3rem

Numbers we will defend

--step-2 · h3 · 1.22–1.55rem

Native woodland

--step-1 · lead · 1.08–1.24rem · 1.62

--step-0 · body · 1.0–1.06rem · 1.62

Most reforestation is funded by people a long way from the land. We do it the other way round: the farm earns, the woodland grows, and the people who plant it live twenty minutes away.

--font-serif · quotations only

A hedge takes seven years to be worth looking at and thirty to be worth counting.

--font-mono · data, labels, years

04

Space & radius

Spacing runs on a 4px base with a soft exponential curve. Section rhythm is fluid between 3rem and 6.5rem, and the gap between panels is a single --page-margin token.

--sp-2 · 8px

--sp-4 · 16px

--sp-6 · 32px

--sp-8 · 64px

The panel system

Every page is a vertical stack of rounded panels on warm paper. A section is the panel — there is no wrapper markup — so a page author only chooses its tone.

.section

White. The default.

.section-alt

Paper tint, for alternating rhythm.

.section-deep

Forest 900, for a hard stop.

--page-margin: clamp(0.4rem, 0.9vw, 1rem); /* paper visible around each panel */
--panel-max: 1660px;
--section-x: clamp(1.15rem, 0.35rem + 3.6vw, 4.75rem); /* panel padding */
--r-panel: clamp(18px, 1.9vw, 32px);

--r-sm · 10px

--r-md · 14px

--r-lg · 20px

--r-panel · 18–32px

05

Elevation

Five shadows, all tinted green rather than grey, so cards feel lit by daylight rather than a spotlight. Depth increases with interactivity, never with importance.

--shadow-sm

Resting inputs, sticky header

--shadow-md

Buttons on hover

--shadow-lg

Cards on hover, hero shell

--shadow-xl

Toasts, floating panels

06

Iconography

One family: 24×24 grid, 1.75px stroke, round caps and joins, no fills. Icons inherit currentColor so they work in every theme without a second asset.

leaf

sprout

tree

drop

users

shield

chart

target

recycle

calendar

map

hand-coins

Illustrations are procedurally generated SVG scenes (see tools/gen_art.py) — no photography, no external image hosts, and every scene re-renders from the same palette tokens.

0+
Counter component

Accordion

Panels animate with grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr, which keeps the transition smooth without measuring heights in JavaScript. The trigger is a real button with aria-expanded.

Add data-accordion-single to close the others when one opens.

Tabs

Tabs are keyboard-navigable with left and right arrows, and roving tabindex.

Panels fade and rise 18px when they become visible.

Only one panel is in the accessibility tree at a time — the rest use the hidden attribute.

Feedback

Success message state
Inline note — for context that supports the surrounding copy.
08

Forms & capture

Every form on the site runs through one handler: validate on blur, describe errors in words, never rely on colour alone, and confirm success politely. Add data-capture="type" to a form and it is wired up.

Hints sit below the control.

Enter a valid email address, e.g. name@example.com

<!-- a fully wired capture form -->
<form data-capture="newsletter" data-redirect="thank-you.html">
  <input name="email" type="email" required>
  <button type="submit">Join</button>
</form>

Submissions are validated, stored in localStorage and replayed on the confirmation page. Set Rootstock.Forms.config.endpoint to POST them to a real collector instead — no markup changes.

09

Motion

Motion explains change: where something came from, that it responds to you, or that it has left. Five durations, four easings, and one absolute rule — all of it disappears under prefers-reduced-motion.

Durations

--dur-1 160ms · state change
--dur-2 280ms · hover, buttons
--dur-3 450ms · panels, cards
--dur-4 700ms · entrances
--dur-5 1.1s · headline wipes, image zoom

Easings

--ease-out · general interface
--ease-expo · entrances, long travel
--ease-spring · anything that should feel alive
--ease-in-out · looping ambient motion

"fade"

Opacity only

"left"

Slide from the left

"right"

Slide from the right

"zoom"

Scale from 0.94

"blur"

Defocus to sharp

Exit & hover

Tilt

Pointer-tracked 3D tilt on cards. data-tilt

Magnetic

Buttons drift toward the cursor. data-magnetic

Exit

With data-reveal-exit, elements soften to 12% opacity as they leave the top of the viewport.

Reduced motion: every transition, parallax, marquee, page transition and counter animation is disabled, and revealed content is shown immediately. Nothing is ever hidden behind an animation that will not run.
10

Accessibility standards

RuleStandard applied
Text contrast4.5:1 minimum, both themes; large text 3:1
Focus2px solid brand outline, 3px offset, never removed
Touch targets44×44px on buttons and form controls; 24×24px minimum on inline text links (WCAG 2.2 AA)
MotionFully disabled under prefers-reduced-motion
FormsReal labels, text errors, aria-invalid, polite status region
LandmarksOne main, labelled navs, skip link on every page
ImagesMeaningful alt text; decorative art marked aria-hidden
KeyboardTabs, accordions, drawer and carousel all operable

The public commitment version of this table lives on the accessibility statement, including what still needs work.

11

Using the system

The whole site is three files plus content. There is no framework and no build step for the CSS or JavaScript.

assets/css/style.cssTokens, components, motion. The only stylesheet.
assets/fonts/*.woff2Plus Jakarta Sans, self-hosted as one variable file per subset.
assets/js/site.jsTheme, nav, reveals, counters, tabs, accordions, carousel, parallax.
assets/js/forms.jsValidation, capture, donation calculator, confirmation page.
tools/build.pyWraps src/*.html fragments in the shared header and footer.
tools/gen_art.pyRegenerates every illustration from the palette.
# edit a page, then
python3 tools/build.py
# change the palette, then
python3 tools/gen_art.py

Privacy policy

Last updated 1 August 2026. Written in plain English, because a policy nobody can read protects nobody.

On this page

Who we are What we collect Why we collect it Who we share it with How long we keep it Your rights Security Complaints
The short version: we collect the minimum we need to send you what you asked for and to claim Gift Aid. We have never sold, rented or swapped a supporter list, and we never will.

1. Who we are

Rootstock Farm & Forest CIC ("Rootstock", "we", "us") is a community interest company registered in England & Wales, company number 11902847, at Cwm Aeron Farm, Hay-on-Wye, Powys HR3 5QA. We are the data controller for the personal data described here. Our data protection contact is privacy@rootstock.earth.

2. What we collect

We only ever collect data you type into a form on this site, plus a small amount of technical data your browser sends automatically.

  • Contact details — name, email address, and where you provide them, phone number and postal address.
  • Donation details — the amount, frequency, chosen project, any dedication message, and whether you have claimed Gift Aid. Card details are handled entirely by our payment provider and never reach our servers.
  • Volunteering details — the session you booked, group size and any access or dietary needs you tell us about. Health-related access needs are special category data and we keep them only until the session has taken place.
  • Partnership enquiries — company name, job context, and what you wrote in the message field.
  • Technical data — IP address, browser type and pages visited, in aggregate, for security and to understand which pages are useful.

We do not use tracking pixels, advertising cookies, or third-party analytics that build a profile of you across other websites. See our cookie policy.

3. Why we collect it, and our lawful basis

What we doWhyLawful basis
Process a donation and send a receiptTo do the thing you asked us to doContract
Claim Gift Aid on your giftHMRC requires name and addressLegal obligation
Send the monthly updateYou ticked the boxConsent
Run a planting day safelyAccess needs, headcount, emergency contactLegitimate interests / explicit consent for health data
Reply to your messageYou wrote to usLegitimate interests
Keep the site securePreventing abuse and fraudLegitimate interests

4. Who we share it with

A short list, and it stays short:

  • Our payment provider, to take payments securely.
  • Our email provider, to send the updates you asked for.
  • HMRC, where you have claimed Gift Aid.
  • Our accountants and auditors, where required to verify our published figures.

Each of these acts as a processor under a written contract and may only use your data on our instructions. We do not transfer personal data outside the UK or EEA except where a provider is covered by adequacy regulations or equivalent safeguards.

5. How long we keep it

  • Donation records: seven years, as required by HMRC for Gift Aid.
  • Newsletter subscriptions: until you unsubscribe, plus 30 days.
  • Volunteer access and health information: deleted within 30 days of the session.
  • General enquiries: two years from your last contact with us.
  • Website server logs: 90 days.

6. Your rights

Under the UK GDPR you have the right to be informed, of access, to rectification, to erasure, to restrict processing, to data portability, and to object — including an absolute right to object to direct marketing. Where we rely on consent, you may withdraw it at any time without affecting anything we did before you withdrew it.

To exercise any of these, email privacy@rootstock.earth. We respond within one month, usually within a week, and we do not charge for it.

7. Security

The site is served over HTTPS. Access to supporter data is limited to the three staff who need it, protected by multi-factor authentication, and reviewed every quarter. If a breach occurs that is likely to result in a risk to your rights, we will notify the ICO within 72 hours and tell you directly without undue delay.

8. Complaints

Tell us first if you can — privacy@rootstock.earth — and we will try to put it right. You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113.

9. Changes to this policy

If we change anything material we will say so on this page and, where the change affects how we use data you have already given us, email you about it. The date at the top always reflects the current version.

Terms of use

Last updated 1 August 2026. These terms apply to everyone who uses this site, gives us money, or turns up with a spade.

On this page

Agreement Using the site Donations Volunteering Partnerships Environmental claims Intellectual property Liability Governing law

1. Agreement

This site is operated by Rootstock Farm & Forest CIC, company number 11902847, registered at Cwm Aeron Farm, Hay-on-Wye, Powys HR3 5QA. By using the site you accept these terms. If you do not accept them, please do not use the site.

2. Using the site

You may use this site for lawful purposes only. You must not attempt to gain unauthorised access to it, introduce malicious code, scrape it at a rate that degrades service for others, or misrepresent your identity when submitting a form. We may suspend access where we reasonably believe any of these has occurred.

We try to keep the site available and accurate, but we do not guarantee uninterrupted availability, and we may change or withdraw any part of it without notice.

3. Donations

  • All donations are made in pounds sterling and are voluntary.
  • Because a donation is a gift, it is generally non-refundable. If you make a mistake — a duplicate payment, the wrong amount, an unintended recurring gift — tell us within 60 days and we will refund it without argument.
  • Monthly gifts continue until you cancel. You may cancel at any time from any email we send you, by replying to us, or through your own bank.
  • Gift Aid may only be claimed where you are a UK taxpayer who has paid at least as much Income or Capital Gains Tax in the tax year as we will reclaim. Tell us if your circumstances change.
  • We allocate restricted gifts to the project you choose. If that project is fully funded or becomes unviable, we will use your gift for the most similar work and tell you we have done so.

4. Volunteering and site visits

A farm is a working environment with vehicles, livestock, uneven ground and weather. When you attend a planting day or open day you agree to follow the safety briefing and the instructions of our site leads, to supervise any children in your care, and to tell us in advance about health or access needs that affect what you can safely do.

Volunteering with Rootstock does not create a contract of employment or a worker relationship, and no payment is due for volunteer time. We may cancel a session at short notice for weather, ground conditions or safety, and will offer you an alternative date.

5. Partnerships and sponsorship

Corporate partnerships are governed by a separate written agreement. Nothing on this site constitutes an offer capable of acceptance. Use of the Rootstock name or logo in your own materials requires our prior written approval, which we give readily where the claim being made is accurate.

6. Environmental claims

This section matters more than the rest. Please read it.

We do not sell carbon offsets and no donation, sponsorship or partnership with us may be described as offsetting, neutralising or compensating for emissions. Our planting is validated under the Woodland Carbon Code, which means the sequestration figures we publish are measured against a recognised standard — not that units have been issued to you.

You may accurately say that you have funded a stated number of trees, or supported a named project. You may not say that your product, event, journey or organisation is "carbon neutral", "net zero" or "climate positive" as a result. If we see a partner making such a claim we will ask for it to be corrected, and end the partnership if it is not.

Projected sequestration figures are estimates over a stated period, dependent on survival and growth. Actual outcomes vary and we publish the variance annually.

7. Intellectual property

The content of this site — text, illustrations, photographs and code — belongs to Rootstock or our contributors, except where stated. You may quote and link to it freely with attribution. Our planting handbook and plot dataset are published deliberately for reuse; you may copy, adapt and redistribute those for any purpose, including commercially, provided you do not misrepresent them as your own data.

8. Liability

Nothing in these terms limits our liability for death or personal injury caused by our negligence, for fraud, or for anything else that cannot lawfully be limited. Subject to that, we are not liable for indirect or consequential loss, and our total liability arising from your use of this site is limited to £1,000 or the amount you have given us in the preceding twelve months, whichever is greater.

Where this site links to other websites, we do not control them and are not responsible for their content.

9. Governing law and changes

These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction. We may update these terms; the version published here at the time you use the site is the one that applies. Material changes are announced on this page for 30 days before taking effect.

Questions about any of this: hello@rootstock.earth.

Cookie policy

Last updated 1 August 2026. There is no cookie banner on this site, because there is nothing to consent to.

We set no advertising cookies, no tracking cookies and no third-party analytics. Everything below is stored in your own browser and never sent to us.

What we store, and why

NameTypePurposeExpires
rootstock:themeLocal storageRemembers whether you chose the light or dark theme.Until you clear it
rootstock:leadsLocal storageHolds a copy of forms you submitted on this demo build, so the confirmation page can show them back to you.Until you clear it

Both are strictly functional: they store a preference you set, on the device you set it on. Under the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations, storage that is strictly necessary to provide a service you have requested does not require consent — which is why you have not been asked to click anything.

What we deliberately do not use

  • No Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, or any other third-party tracker.
  • No advertising or remarketing cookies. We do not run ads.
  • No embedded content that sets cookies without asking — videos are self-hosted.
  • No cross-site fingerprinting, session recording or heat mapping.

We measure how the site is doing from anonymised server logs, which record the page requested, an approximate region and a truncated IP address, kept for 90 days. Those logs cannot identify you.

How to clear what is stored

  1. Open your browser settings and find "Privacy", "Site settings" or "Cookies and site data".
  2. Search for this site's address.
  3. Choose "Remove" or "Clear data".

Clearing it resets the theme to your system preference and empties the local copy of any form you submitted. Nothing else changes, and nothing breaks.

Payments

When a live payment provider is connected, its checkout may set its own strictly necessary cookies to process your transaction securely and prevent fraud. Those are governed by that provider's own policy, which we will link here at the point it goes live.

Changes

If we ever add anything that is not strictly necessary — and we have no plans to — we will ask for your consent first, and this page will say so before it happens.

Questions: privacy@rootstock.earth.

Accessibility statement

Last reviewed 1 August 2026. This covers both the website and visiting the farm itself.

How accessible this website is

We aim to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA. In practice that means:

  • Every page works with a keyboard alone, with a visible focus outline and a skip link to the main content.
  • Text contrast meets or exceeds 4.5:1 in both the light and dark themes.
  • All motion — scroll reveals, parallax, marquees, page transitions — is switched off automatically when your device requests reduced motion.
  • Text resizes to 200% without loss of content, and the layout reflows to a single column on narrow screens.
  • Images that carry meaning have alternative text; decorative illustrations are hidden from screen readers.
  • Forms use real labels, describe their errors in text as well as colour, and announce success politely.

What we know is not perfect yet

  • The project carousel can be scrolled with arrow buttons and a trackpad, but does not yet respond to arrow keys when focus is inside the track.
  • Our downloadable impact report PDF is not fully tagged. We will publish an HTML version alongside it in the 2026 edition.
  • Some data tables are wide and scroll horizontally on small screens.

These are on our list, and we would rather say so than pretend otherwise.

Visiting the farm

  • Level, firm-surfaced access to the farm shop, the barn and the first 400m of the riverside trail.
  • An accessible WC with grab rails and a level threshold, next to the shop.
  • Designated parking within 20m of the shop entrance.
  • Assistance dogs are welcome everywhere on the farm.
  • Seated planting stations at every volunteer day, on level ground, with raised beds for nursery work.
  • Black Hill and the upper Aeron plots are steep, rough and not currently wheelchair accessible. We will always find you an alternative site on the same day.

Tell us when we get it wrong

If something on this site or at the farm is difficult to use, email access@rootstock.earth or call +44 (0)1497 555 118. We aim to reply within two working days and to fix website issues within 30 days.

If you need any information from this site in another format — large print, plain text, audio or an easy-read summary — ask and we will send it within ten working days, free.

Enforcement

If you are not happy with how we respond, you can contact the Equality Advisory and Support Service (EASS). We take that route seriously and would much rather resolve it with you directly first.
